key_insight: Oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group oxides are largely explained by crystal reduction potential and band gap, linking defect energetics to cation reducibility.
engineering_relevance: The model estimates vacancy formation energies from bulk properties, potentially supporting oxide screening for energy technologies rather than directly predicting solar-cell performance.
method: Surveyed 39 binary oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Used ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed neutral oxygen-vacancy ground states.
Fit an interpretable model retaining reduction potential and band gap.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: The study covers neutral vacancies in binary main-group oxides; transfer to charged defects or perovskite solar-cell materials requires validation.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
